en.t: What on earth are they planning?
... Is it meant as a bargain?

units.source_text: ……听说印第安人把香烟作为友好的信物来交换。

en.t: ... They say Indians exchange cigarettes as tokens of friendship.

units.source_text: 酒一般也作为祝贺的标志。

en.t: Alcohol, too, is generally a sign of celebration.

units.source_text: 难道可以认为对方有妥协的意思，以这种形式先来表示一下吗？

en.t: Could he take it to mean that the other side intended to compromise, and was first showing it in this form?

units.source_text: 乡下人用语言来表达心情老有害臊的倾向。

en.t: Country people always tend to feel embarrassed about putting their feelings into words.

units.source_text: 也就是说，只有这点可说他们是老实人。

en.t: In other words, this was the one respect in which they could be called honest people.
